relations.definition: To have gone through or undergone a particular event or situation.
relations.embedding_query_text: experienced: To have gone through or undergone a particular event or situation.

chosen_property.label: experiencedEvent
chosen_property.definition: To have undergone or been affected by an event or situation.

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: experienceRequirements
candidates.comment: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: monthsOfExperience
candidates.comment: A required number of months of experience for an occupational role. Also called experience duration, minimum experience, required experience in months. Examples: "Software Engineer Role monthsOfExperience 24", "Marketing Manager Position monthsOfExperience 60", "Entry-level Job monthsOfExperience 0".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: To have given an account or description of something, typically in an official or formal manner.
relations.embedding_query_text: reported: To have given an account or description of something, typically in an official or formal manner.

chosen_property.label: reportedEvent
chosen_property.definition: To have given an account or description of something, typically in an official or formal manner.

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: legalName
candidates.comment: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: bookEdition
candidates.comment: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: responsibilities
candidates.comment: A description of the duties and tasks associated with a job posting or occupation. Also called duties, tasks, job functions, accountabilities. Examples: `Software Engineer Job Posting` responsibilities `"Develop and maintain web applications"`, `Marketing Manager Occupation` responsibilities `"Oversee campaign strategy"`, `Doctor Job` responsibilities `"Diagnose and treat patients"`.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

relations.definition: To have happened or taken place at a specific time or period.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred during: To have happened or taken place at a specific time or period.

chosen_property.label: occurredDuring
chosen_property.definition: To have happened or taken place at a specific time or period.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: temporalCoverage
candidates.comment: A temporal scope relation between a creative work and the specific time period that its content describes or applies to. Also called "time period covered", "content timeframe", "temporal scope", "date range of content". Examples: "A census dataset has temporalCoverage 2011/2012", "The historical novel's temporalCoverage is 1939/1945", "This research paper's temporalCoverage is 2015-11/..". Distinct from temporal, which is a more general temporal association when the specific scope is not known.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

relations.definition: To have happened or taken place in a specific location or context.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred in: To have happened or taken place in a specific location or context.

chosen_property.label: occurredInYear
chosen_property.definition: To have happened or taken place in a specific year.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: artist
candidates.comment: A person who is the primary creator of a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork, especially in non-line art mediums. Also called: creator, illustrator, visual creator. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Starry Night' artist 'Vincent van Gogh'", "ComicIssue 'Issue #1' artist 'Frank Miller'", "ComicStory 'Origin Story' artist 'Alex Ross'". Distinct from author, which is a more general term for the creator of content, often textual.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedAnatomy
candidates.comment: A related anatomy relation between superficial anatomy and other anatomical structures or systems connected to it. Also called associated anatomy, connected to anatomy. Examples: "The skin of the forearm has related anatomy 'radius bone'.", "The superficial muscles of the back have related anatomy 'vertebral column'.", "The scalp has related anatomy 'cranium'."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

chosen_property.label: recordedValue
chosen_property.definition: To have been captured or documented in some way.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: track
candidates.comment: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: audio
candidates.comment: An embedded audio object associated with a creative work. Also called: audio file, sound recording, soundtrack. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Podcast Episode' audio 'AudioObject of Episode'", "CreativeWork 'Movie' audio 'Soundtrack Clip'", "CreativeWork 'Webpage' audio 'Background Music'."

candidates.label: musicReleaseFormat
candidates.comment: The format of a music release, indicating the type of recording media. Also called release format, media type, recording format. Examples: "Album X musicReleaseFormat 'CDFormat'", "Single Y musicReleaseFormat 'DigitalAudioTapeFormat'", "LP Z musicReleaseFormat 'VinylFormat'".

candidates.label: recordLabel
candidates.comment: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: eligibilityToWorkRequirement
candidates.comment: An eligibility to work requirement relation between a job posting and the text describing the legal documentation needed for an applicant. Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: endOffset
candidates.comment: An end offset relation between a clip and the number or HyperTocEntry representing its end time from the beginning of the work. Also called "clip end time", "segment end", "finish offset". Examples: "Video clip endOffset '120' (seconds)", "Audio segment endOffset 'HyperTocEntry for Chapter 5'", "Media clip endOffset '300'". Distinct from endTime, which is a more general property for the end time of various items, including actions and media objects.

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.
